part: Section 4: Sentence Completion / Academic lecture (single speaker)
instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer.

tasks.transcript: Today's lecture examines the history of coffee cultivation. Coffee is believed to have originated in the Ethiopian highlands, where local legend credits a goat herder named Kaldi with discovering its stimulating effects. From there, cultivation spread to the Arabian Peninsula, particularly Yemen, by the fifteenth century, where it became central to social and religious life. By the seventeenth century, coffee houses had spread across Europe, becoming important hubs for intellectual discussion, often nicknamed 'penny universities' because a cup of coffee cost only a penny and granted access to hours of stimulating conversation. Today, Brazil is the world's largest producer, accounting for roughly a third of global coffee output.

tasks.transcript: This lecture focuses on the development of public transportation in the nineteenth century. The first underground railway opened in London in 1863, primarily to reduce street-level congestion caused by horse-drawn traffic. Early trains were powered by steam locomotives, which created significant ventilation problems in the tunnels. It wasn't until the introduction of electric trains in the 1890s that underground travel became significantly more comfortable and practical. Other major cities, including Budapest and Paris, followed London's example, building their own underground systems by the turn of the century. Today, over 160 cities worldwide operate metro systems, carrying billions of passengers annually.
